requirements.quote: To initiate path validation, an endpoint sends a PATH_CHALLENGE frame containing an unpredictable payload on the path to be validated.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint initiates path validation.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a PATH_CHALLENGE frame containing an unpredictable payload on the path being validated.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can initiate path validation and inspect the selected path and the emitted frame type and payload.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MAY send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames to guard against packet loss.
requirements.condition: When guarding path validation against packet loss.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames to be sent.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can verify that the implementation permits transmission of multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames during path validation.

requirements.quote: However, an endpoint SHOULD NOT send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames in a single packet.
requirements.condition: When constructing a packet containing PATH_CHALLENGE frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames in one packet unless a justified exception to the SHOULD NOT applies.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet inspection can count the PATH_CHALLENGE frames contained in each packet.

requirements.quote: An endpoint SHOULD NOT probe a new path with packets containing a PATH_CHALLENGE frame more frequently than it would send an Initial packet.
requirements.condition: When probing a new path using packets that contain PATH_CHALLENGE frames.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit the probing frequency to no more than the endpoint's Initial-packet sending frequency unless a justified exception to the SHOULD NOT applies.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send such path probes more frequently than Initial packets would be sent unless a justified exception applies.
requirements.why_checkable: A timing test can compare the implementation's PATH_CHALLENGE probe rate with its Initial-packet transmission rate.

requirements.quote: The endpoint MUST use unpredictable data in every PATH_CHALLENGE frame so that it can associate the peer's response with the corresponding PATH_CHALLENGE.
requirements.condition: Whenever an endpoint constructs a PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use unpredictable data in every PATH_CHALLENGE frame, enabling the corresponding peer response to be associated with that challenge.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use predictable challenge data or omit unpredictable data from any PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated PATH_CHALLENGE payloads can be inspected for use of the implementation's unpredictable-data mechanism and response-to-challenge association.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MUST expand datagrams that contain a PATH_CHALLENGE frame to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes, unless the anti-amplification limit for the path does not permit sending a datagram of this size.
requirements.condition: When sending a datagram containing a PATH_CHALLENGE frame and the path's anti-amplification limit permits a 1200-byte datagram.
requirements.required_behavior: Expand the datagram to at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send the PATH_CHALLENGE datagram below 1200 bytes when the anti-amplification limit permits that size.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can measure each qualifying PATH_CHALLENGE datagram and evaluate the anti-amplification allowance for its path.

requirements.quote: When an endpoint is unable to expand the datagram size to 1200 bytes due to the anti-amplification limit, the path MTU will not be validated.
requirements.condition: When the anti-amplification limit prevents an endpoint from expanding a PATH_CHALLENGE datagram to 1200 bytes.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the path MTU in an unvalidated state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat the path MTU as validated based on that undersized datagram.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-based test can force the anti-amplification exception and verify that path-MTU validation is not recorded.

requirements.quote: To ensure that the path MTU is large enough, the endpoint MUST perform a second path validation by sending a PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a datagram of at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.condition: After an initial path validation used a PATH_CHALLENGE datagram smaller than 1200 bytes because of the anti-amplification limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Perform a second path validation by sending a PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a datagram of at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not consider the required path-MTU validation complete without the second validation using a datagram of at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can trigger the undersized anti-amplification case and verify a subsequent validation attempt and its datagram size.

requirements.quote: Unlike other cases where datagrams are expanded, endpoints MUST NOT discard datagrams that appear to be too small when they contain PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE.
requirements.condition: When a datagram appears too small but contains a PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Retain the datagram for normal handling despite its apparent small size.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not discard the datagram merely because it appears too small.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver apparently undersized datagrams containing either frame type and observe whether the implementation discards them for size alone.
